subject.description: Agent (service account agent-svc) on Group Open Banking Gateway that fulfils inbound account information requests from registered third party providers: retrieves request, consent and recipient, scopes and assembles a data package, requests human release authorisation, and transmits. Documents describe the process as AIS-RPA-014; see identity finding F-00.

claim.statement: On the evidence supplied, ta-ob-2 operates at autonomy tier T2 (asserted on configuration alone; approval quality not assessed because the only approval records are simulated) within open banking account information sharing for registered third party providers against active customer consents (90-day data window, one transmission per run), may read and retrieve (A1), analyse (A2), recommend or route (A4), write internally (A5) and transmit data externally to the consented recipient (A7), is prohibited from drafting for a person (A3, allowlisted but no tool), internal commit (A6), bounded transactions (A8), moving funds (A9), regulatory filing (A10), access or infrastructure change (A11) and delegation (A12), and operates under least-privilege consented_only credentials, per-case consent-scope, consent-validity and recipient-binding rules that block on failure, a transmission cap, and a human approval gate on every transmit whose approver is not shown the resource; purpose limitation is not enforced in configuration. 6 fields could not be established and 5 conflicts remain open. This is a Level 1 Asserted Profile: nothing in it has been tested.

modifiers.data_authority: Reads customer account data, consent records, TPP registration records and inbound requests (incl. attachments) through gateway tools under service account agent-svc scoped consented_only; writes only internal notes and release packages; discloses assembled data to third parties via transmit.
modifiers.reversibility_profile: Mixed: reads and analysis n/a; internal writes (add_note, prepare_package) reversible; transmit (A7) discloses customer data to an external third party and cannot be recalled once released.
modifiers.customer_market_impact: Direct customer impact: an erroneous release discloses a customer's account data to a third party outside the customer's consent (data-protection and conduct exposure). No market impact identified.
modifiers.accountability: Documents name First Line (Open Banking Operations) as process and authorisation-queue owner, with Second Line (Operational Risk, MRM) challenge and Third Line assurance. Accountable owner for this Profile: <named accountable owner>, Head of Open Banking (to confirm against the documented process owner role, Head of Open Banking Operations).
modifiers.population_scope: Customers of the Group holding an active account-information consent with a registered third party provider; agent account scope restricted to consented_only. Population size not stated.

autonomy.tier.note: T2 is ASSERTED on configuration alone: the agent chains a multi-step task (run log) and every transmit requires approval (approval="always"). No real approval records exist to substantiate it (the only records are simulated; see conflict C1). Two indications point away from T2: (a) the simulated records, if real, would show reflexive approval and an effective tier of T3; (b) the console rendering and the procedure show the approver is NOT shown the specific resource (T2 requires it; see conflict C3). Owner to confirm T2 or record T3.

autonomy.approval_quality.note: not_assessed: the only approval records (e9, n=3) are marked simulated: true in their metadata (e10) and cannot establish approval quality. Recorded values, for information only: n=3, median 1.615 s (range 0.992-1.637 s), edit rate 0/3, rejection rate 0/3, one approver (ops-release-01), one batch (batch_0000), all three share APPROVAL_REF apr_000, approver_shown_resource=false. Had these been real they would have been decisive for reflexive approval, i.e. effective tier T3 rather than T2. The PDF rendering (e11) omits the simulated marker. MRM's statement that CO-5 is 'Effective' on 200 authorisation records (e4) is document_derived and the records are not in the package. Needed: a real (non-simulated) production extract of approval decisions with latency, edits, rejections and what the approver saw.

out_of_scope.statement: This Profile asserts what the institution's documents and exported configuration say is deployed; it tests nothing. It does not establish: that any gateway rule blocks as configured under real or adversarial load; that approvals are substantive (the only records are simulated); that the approver can perform the documented manual purpose check (configuration says the resource is not shown); that purpose limitation is enforced at all; the behaviour or identity of the model the agent calls (no model identity in the package) or the deployment version; the agent's resilience to instructions embedded in request attachments returned by get_request; behaviour of the six ungoverned tools; network egress (not held in the console); immutability or completeness of event records; changes made after the 2026-06-30 change extract; that the documents (which describe AIS-RPA-014) describe this deployment; jurisdictional scope; and payment initiation, which is out of scope of the documented process and prohibited in configuration.

open_findings.note: IDENTITY: only the simulated approval extract (e9-e11) names deployment ta-ob-2. All documents describe AIS-RPA-014 on Group Open Banking Gateway, and MRM (June 2026) describes it as 'not a model in the quantitative sense' (automated decisioning), while the run log shows model.call and plan events (a model-driven agent). No change record to 2026-06-30 introduces a model. Owner must confirm that the documents, the MRM validation and the configuration exports all describe ta-ob-2 as deployed; otherwise document_derived fields and the MRM attestation do not apply.
C1 simulated approval records; tier T2 rests on configuration alone.
C2 purpose limitation claimed gateway-enforced; not configured.
C3 approver not shown resource; batch 20; 1.2 s target.
C4 caps stricter than any documented mandate.
C5 reconstruction claimed; event extract lacks identifiers.
A3 is on the gateway Permitted list but no tool or entitlement exists in class A3: allowlist entry with no tool. Recorded as prohibited as built.
Six tools run under rule default-allow, onFail none, reason UNGOVERNED: add_note, escalate, evaluate_scope, get_recipient, refuse, request_approval (two of them state-changing writes).

Console rendering e8 carries approval-workflow, retention and encryption settings absent from its machine-readable sibling e7; that content is document_derived. Conversely the approval rendering e11 omits the simulated marker present in e10.
Model identity (provider, model, pinned version) and deployment version are absent from the package. The Profile cannot be issued without them (ARP-081).

Workflow event extract (e15) is timestamp-aligned with the simulated approval records (2026-09-05 23:43:19-20, three runs) and may be from the same simulation; it is used only to show the form of logging, not as production corroboration.
